chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Isḥāq from Jaʿfar from his father (peace be upon him) that ʿAlī (peace be upon him) used to say:

When the Muḥrim (person in iḥrām) is compelled to [eat] game and carrion, let him eat the carrion that Allah has permitted him, so as not to contradict the earlier reports, because in the report it is not specified that he was compelled to [eat] game and carrion while he was capable of and able to consume them. And if that is not explicit in its apparent meaning, we interpret it as referring to one who cannot find game nor is able to reach it, but is able to consume carrion; at that time it is permissible for him to consume carrion. As for when game is available and he is able to consume it, then it is not permissible under any condition.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of iḥrām

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Muḥrim who is forced to choose between eating game and eating carrion?
ai.summary: Imam ʿAlī (peace be upon him) clarifies the hierarchy of necessity for a Muḥrim by distinguishing between general reports and specific conditions of access, ruling that carrion is only permissible when game is unavailable or inaccessible. This interpretation by the Shaykh al-Tusi tradition emphasizes the principle of *darura* (necessity) being limited to the extent of the need, ensuring that the prohibition of game remains primary unless physical constraints prevent its consumption.
